wants.topic: Economic and institutional mechanics driving modern war participation (e.g. rural poverty vs. military salaries, coercion, penal recruitment)
wants.evidence: 'Why Russians Still Sign Up to Die' achieved a massive 40.89 vsNormal rating, with top comments heavily discussing the regional purchasing power of soldier pay ($2,500/mo) and institutional recruitment pressure.

wants.topic: Covert intelligence operations, secret military logistics, and international cover-ups
wants.evidence: 'The Israeli Plane Crash Conspiracy' achieved 11.59 vsNormal, with top comments focusing on Mossad presence, unauthorized arms/depleted uranium transport on civilian flights, and missing black boxes.

wants.topic: Institutional failures of global peacekeeping bodies (e.g. UN inaction during genocides)
wants.evidence: 'When a Genocide Was Broadcast Live on TV' generated 8,700+ comments, with viewers aggressively discussing UN bureaucratic absurdity ('cue to run') and peacekeeper passivity in Srebrenica and Rwanda.

wants.topic: Psychological and inner-circle power dynamics of historical dictators
wants.evidence: 'Hitler's Court: The Private World of the Dictator' gained 2.58M views (5.8 vsNormal) by focusing on private court dynamics rather than generic battlefield movements.

gaps: Systemic financial/procedural loopholes used by state militaries to avoid family compensation (e.g., 'Missing in Action' classifications to skip death benefits).
Investigations into 'sniper tourism' and foreign mercenaries in post-Cold War urban sieges.
Comparative analyses of modern state historical denial and how war crimes are scrubbed from national education systems.
saturated: Standard surface-level biographies of political figures (e.g., 'Who Was Dick Cheney?' underperformed severely at 0.1 vsNormal).
Generic broad-brush WWII history overviews lacking a specific psychological, logistical, or covert angle.
Vlog-style or off-niche cultural experiments (e.g., Italian gesture training at 0.01 vsNormal).
